IMPRESSION:
Mild scoliosis convexity to the left. No acute abnormality in the thoracic spine.

FINDINGS:
VERTEBRAE: Normal vertebral body heights are maintained. No acute fracture or focal osseous lesion. Marrow signal is within normal limits for age. A benign-appearing vertebral hemangioma is noted within the L2 vertebral body. Focal marrow/soft-tissue edema-like signal involving the anterior adjacent endplate at L2-L3 and spinous process of L4 correlate clinically and consider further evaluation if clinically indicated.
ALIGNMENT: Anatomic lumbar lordosis is straightened. No spondylolisthesis.
SPINAL CORD: The conus medullaris terminates at a normal level, demonstrating normal signal and contour. The cauda equina nerve roots are unremarkable.
DISCS/DEGENERATIVE CHANGES: Intervertebral disc heights and hydration are preserved. No significant facet arthropathy or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Mild diffuse disc bulge is noted at L1-L2 without significant central canal stenosis or neural foraminal compromise. Diffuse disc bulge is noted at L2-L3 with bilateral neural foraminal narrowing. At L3-L4, diffuse disc bulge with bilateral foraminal extension is noted, causing bilateral neural foraminal narrowing with crowding/impingement of the exiting nerve roots. At L4-L5, diffuse disc bulge with bilateral neural foraminal narrowing is noted. The AP diameter of the central spinal canal measures approximately 9.6 mm, suggestive of mild central canal stenosis. At L5-S1, diffuse disc bulge with bilateral foraminal extension is noted, causing bilateral neural foraminal narrowing and impingement of the exiting nerve roots. The central canal measures approximately 12 mm in AP diameter.
L1-L2: No central canal or foraminal stenosis. The intervertebral disc is normal in appearance.
L2-L3: Diffuse disc bulge with bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
L3-L4: Diffuse disc bulge with bilateral foraminal extension, causing bilateral neural foraminal narrowing with crowding/impingement of the exiting nerve roots.
L4-L5: Diffuse disc bulge with bilateral neural foraminal narrowing. The AP diameter of the central spinal canal measures approximately 9.6 mm, suggestive of mild central canal stenosis.
L5-S1: Diffuse disc bulge with bilateral foraminal extension, causing bilateral neural foraminal narrowing and impingement of the exiting nerve roots.
PARASPINAL SOFT TISSUES: The visualized paravertebral soft tissues are symmetric and without abnormal signal.

IMPRESSION:
Multilevel lumbar spondylotic degenerative changes with multilevel disc bulges. L3-L4 bilateral neural foraminal narrowing with impingement of bilateral exiting nerve roots. L4-L5 disc bulge with mild central canal stenosis (canal AP diameter ~9.6 mm). L5-S1 bilateral foraminal narrowing with impingement of bilateral exiting nerve roots. Benign-appearing vertebral hemangioma in L2. Focal marrow/soft-tissue edema-like signal involving the anterior adjacent endplate at L2-L3 and spinous process of L4 correlate clinically and consider further evaluation if clinically indicated.

FINDINGS:
BONES: No acute fracture or focal lesion. Mild diffuse osmineralization.
JOINTS: No dislocation. The joint spaces and articular margins are normal except for mild degenerative changes of the acromioclavicular joint. Glenohumeral joint space is relatively maintained.
SOFT TISSUES: The soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
Mild diffuse osseous demineralization and mild acromioclavicular osteoarthritis.
